part2.intro: Three young people talk about their favourite colour.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Rosa
texts.text: My favourite colour is orange. It's warm and happy, like the sun! My bedroom walls are orange – Dad and I painted them together last summer. Some people think the colour is too bright, but I love waking up in there. My grandma always buys me orange things for my birthday, and this year she gave me orange trainers. My friends call me 'the orange girl' now!

texts.label: B
texts.title: Minh
texts.text: I've always liked dark blue. Most of my clothes are dark blue or black, because I think they look smart. My mum says I should wear lighter colours sometimes, but I don't agree with her. I also love the sea, and I want to be a diver when I'm older, so I can see the blue water every day. The only red thing I've got is my school bag – it was a present from my uncle.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Freya
texts.text: Green is my favourite colour because I love nature. At the weekends I go walking in the hills with my family and take photos of trees and plants. I've got hundreds of pictures! I don't wear green clothes very often, because I don't think green looks good on me. But my bedroom is full of plants – I've got twenty-three of them, and I give them water every morning before school.

items.q: Who decorated a room with a family member?
Who has a different opinion from a parent about colours?
Who doesn't often wear their favourite colour?
Who has a new name because of their favourite colour?
Who would like a job connected with their favourite colour?

Who got a present in their favourite colour?

part3.title: From grey to great
part3.text:
For years, the long wall behind Greenfield School was grey and ugly. Students walked past it every day without looking at it. Then fourteen-year-old Lena Novak had an idea.

"I asked the head teacher if I could paint a picture on it," says Lena. "She said yes, but only if I could find the money for the paint myself." So Lena and her friends washed cars in the school car park every Saturday for two months. They made one hundred and eighty pounds – enough for twenty tins of paint.

Lena wanted the picture to show the town's river, with green trees, a blue sky and red and yellow birds. "At first I wanted lots of dark colours, like dark green and purple. But my art teacher said light colours would look better because the street is quite narrow. She was right," Lena says.

Painting the wall took three weeks. Thirty students helped, and some parents came to paint after work too. "The hardest part was the sky," Lena explains. "We had to mix white and blue again and again before we got the right colour."

Now people from all over town come to take photos of the wall. The local newspaper wrote a story about it, and the town hospital has asked Lena to paint a wall in its children's area. "I'm going to use lots of yellow, orange and pink there," she says. "Happy colours for children who are ill."

items.q: What did the head teacher say Lena had to do?
options: find the money for the paint

options: She sold some of her paintings.
Her parents gave it to her.
She and her friends washed cars.

items.q: Why did Lena change her mind about the colours?
options: Her teacher gave her some advice.
Her friends didn't like dark colours.

items.q: What was difficult about painting the wall?
options: making the right colour for the sky
painting the birds on the river

items.q: What is Lena going to do next?
options: write a story for the newspaper
paint a picture at a hospital

part4.title: Why are flamingos pink?
part4.text:
Flamingos are famous for their beautiful pink colour. But did you know that baby flamingos are not pink at all? When they are born, they are grey or white. They only {19} pink when they are two or three years old.

So where does the colour come {20}? The answer is food. Flamingos eat very small animals and plants that live in water. These {21} a natural orange-red colour inside them, and slowly this changes the colour of the birds' feathers. If flamingos in a zoo don't get the right food, they become very {22} – almost white!

The colour is also important when flamingos are looking for a partner. Scientists think that the brightest pink birds are the healthiest, so other flamingos usually {23} them. Some flamingos even put a special oil from their bodies on their feathers to make them look pinker – a bit {24} wearing make-up!

part7.instruction: Look at the three pictures. Write the story shown in the pictures. Write 35 words or more.

pictures.caption: a girl painting a garden fence white; a tin of red paint is on the grass
a dog runs through the red paint and leaves red footprints all over the white fence
the girl has painted green stems under the red footprints so they look like flowers; her dad is smiling

part7.model: Last Sunday Mai was painting the garden fence white. Suddenly her dog ran across the garden, put its feet in a tin of red paint and jumped up at the fence. There were red footprints everywhere! Mai had an idea. She painted green lines under them, and they looked like beautiful flowers. Her dad loved it.

items.q: Which T-shirt does the boy buy?

script.t: I like this T-shirt, but which colour should I get? Red or green?
You've already got lots of red clothes. What about this grey one?
Grey's a bit boring. I'll take the green one. It goes well with my jeans.
Good choice.

items.q: What colour is the girl's new bike?

script.t: I got my new bike today!
Great! Is it pink, like your old one?
No, I wanted something different. I nearly chose a white one, but white gets dirty so quickly. So I got a purple one, with black wheels.
Cool! Let's go for a ride.

items.q: Where are the girl's paints?

script.t: Dad, where are my paints? They aren't in my black bag.
Did you look in the brown box under your desk?
Yes, but there are only pencils in there.
Oh, sorry, I remember now. I put them on the shelf in the kitchen, next to the radio.

items.q: What is the boy painting?

script.t: What are you painting, Tom? Is it the sea? There's so much blue.
No, the blue is the sky. Look, this is the orange sun. It's going down behind the hills.
Oh, it's a sunset! I thought those dark green shapes were trees.
No, they're hills. Maybe I'll add some trees later.

items.q: Which is Mia's dog?

script.t: Look, that's my dog in this photo.
Which one? The brown one?
No, that's my neighbour's dog. Mine is the white one with black ears.
Oh, and who's the black one with white ears? They look the same!
That's his brother. He lives with my cousin.

part2.intro: You will hear a woman talking about a colour run for charity.
part2.title: Hillside Colour Run

script.t: Hello, and thanks for coming. I'm here to tell you about the Hillside Colour Run. It's a fun run where people throw coloured powder at you while you run! It's on Sunday the twelfth of June. We wanted to have it in May, but the park was already busy then. Don't worry – you don't have to be a fast runner. The run is five kilometres. Last year it was ten, but lots of people told us that was too long. At every kilometre there's a different colour: first red, then yellow, then blue, then green. And at the finish, everyone gets covered in purple! So please wear white clothes – you'll look like a rainbow at the end. Tickets for adults are fifteen pounds. If you're under sixteen, it's eight pounds, and you get a free T-shirt too. All the money goes to the children's hospital. The run starts at Wickham Park. That's W-I-C-K-H-A-M. It's next to the railway station. Please arrive at nine o'clock. And one more thing: bring some sunglasses to keep the powder out of your eyes!

part3.intro: You will hear Oliver talking to his friend Hannah about a school trip to an art gallery.

Oliver's favourite painting was
In the afternoon, the students
What did Oliver buy in the gift shop?
What will the next exhibition be about?

script.t: Hi Oliver. How was the school trip to the art gallery?
Really good, Hannah! I thought it would be boring, but it wasn't at all.
What did you see?
There were lots of old paintings of kings and queens, but they were very dark – mostly brown and black. My favourite was a modern one. It was just a big yellow circle on a light blue background.
That sounds easy! I could paint that.
That's what everyone said! But the guide told us the artist painted it in 1960, and now it's worth millions.
Did you do anything else?
Yes, in the afternoon there was a class. We wanted to paint, but there wasn't enough time, so we made pictures with coloured paper instead. I made a green and orange fish.
Cool. Did you buy anything in the gift shop?
The postcards were really expensive, and I've already got lots of pens. So I bought a poster of the yellow circle for my bedroom wall. It was only three pounds.
Are you going to go back?
Yes! Next month there's a new exhibition all about the colour red – red clothes, red paintings, even red food! My mum wants to go, and you can come with us if you like.
I'd love to. But not on a Saturday – I've got swimming.
That's fine. We'll go on a Sunday.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking to his mother about his bedroom.
items.q: Why does he want to change the colour of his room?
options: It makes the room look small.
He doesn't like blue any more.

script.t: Mum, can we paint my bedroom a different colour?
But you chose that dark blue only last year! You said blue was your favourite colour.
It still is. My friends think the room's cool, too. But it's so dark – it feels tiny, like a cupboard. I'd like something lighter, like white or light grey.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her friend about a birthday present.
items.q: How does the girl feel about the present?

script.t: My aunt gave me a sweater for my birthday. It's bright pink with big yellow spots.
Wow! Did you know she was going to give you clothes?
Yes, she always does. She was so pleased with it, so I said thank you. But I'll never wear it – I only like black and grey clothes. I really wanted some new headphones.

items.intro: You will hear a teacher talking to her class.
items.q: What does the teacher want the students to do?

script.t: Tomorrow we're going to start painting the big picture for the school hall. We'll use lots of paint, especially red and black, and they're very difficult to wash out. So please bring an old shirt or T-shirt to wear over your uniform. Don't worry about paint or brushes – I've got everything we need. And we'll all clean the room together at the end.

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a film.
items.q: What did the boy like most about the film?

script.t: Did you enjoy the film last night?
Well, the story was a bit silly, and the music was much too loud.
Oh dear. So you didn't like it?
I did, actually, because it looked amazing. Every part had different colours – purple forests, orange seas, pink mountains. I've never seen anything like it.

items.intro: You will hear a woman talking on the radio about a garden.
items.q: Why do most people visit the garden in May?

script.t: Hillcrest Garden is lovely all year, but May is the best time to visit. That's when thousands of flowers open – red, yellow, white, and even dark purple ones that look almost black. People come from all over the country to see them. You can have a picnic by the lake, but please don't pick the flowers. And the garden shop sells plants, but only in the autumn.

part5.intro: You will hear Lily talking to her friend Ben about sports day. What colour T-shirt will each team wear?

script.t: Lily, do you know the team colours for sports day yet?
Yes, Mr Price told us this morning. You're in the Lions, aren't you? You wanted yellow, but the Lions are orange this year.
Orange? Oh well, it's quite like yellow. What about your team, the Eagles?
We all wanted black, but the teachers said it's too hot to wear black in the sun. So we've got purple.
Purple's nice. And the Dolphins? Blue, I suppose, like the sea?
That's what everyone thought! But no, they're green. Blue is for the Bears.
That's strange. Bears are brown!
I know, but the shop didn't have any brown T-shirts. Dark blue was the closest colour, Mr Price said.
And the Tigers? My sister's in that team. She said they asked for pink.
They did, but some of the boys weren't happy about it. So in the end they chose red. It looks really good with the white shorts.
So everyone wears white shorts?
Yes, and white socks. By the end of the day they'll be grey, I'm sure!
